title: Burst attribution heatmap + annotations (working)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note for decomposing short-duration burst events into actionable root causes and showing a compact, text-first heatmap for product reviews. The goal is to have a reproducible, low-effort artifact engineers and SREs can use to quickly determine whether a burst is driven by workload mix, cold starts, KV-cache miss storms, tenant interference, or infra noise (network/IO).

Summary (single-paragraph):
We ran three controlled replays and two live-sampled bursts against the same Dedicated pool (g5-32x, Q4-quant profile, kvcache enabled) to attribute p75/p95/p99 shifts to four candidate drivers. Results show that ~60% of observed p99 spike magnitude during short bursts (30s–3m) aligns with session-mix amplification (long-turn sessions + prompt priming). KV-cache miss storms explain ~25% of token-level tail, and cold-start waves accounted for the remaining variance in the smallest tests. Tenant interference was measurable but smaller than expected on this workload. A compact heatmap (below) encodes combined severity and cost delta.

Methodology (short):
- Baseline: steady-state replay (800 qps equivalent) for 10m to capture normal percentiles and cost.
- Controlled bursts: 3 shapes (fast-spike 10s 5x, sustained-surge 90s 2x, sawtooth 3m oscillating 3x->1x) replayed from recorded prod traces.
- Variations toggled per-burst: kvcache on/off, prewarm pool true/false, tenant-isolation (soft shares 0.7/0.3), quant profile (Q4 vs Q2).
- Metrics: p50/p75/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost-per-1k-tokens computed from allocation time and instance unit price.
- Repeat each variation 3x, take median.

Testbed config (concise):
- Pool: dedicated-east-1-g5-32x, 16 nodes, 512GB RAM, NVMe stripe.
- Model: open-7b-v2 (preforked weights), sequence cap 1024, kv cache sized 48GB.
- Runtime: serving-runtime@sha:8c9f2b (kernel selection v3), batching window 4ms, dynamic-slot-tiling enabled.
- Cost math: instance cost $7.20/hr (apex estimate), amortized tokens counted across run.

Annotated heatmap (text grid):
Legend: 0=no effect | + = small | ++ = medium | +++ = large | $ = cost increase indicator
Rows = drivers, Cols = burst shapes (fast, sustained, sawtooth), Cells = impact / cost

            | fast-spike | sustained | sawtooth
session-mix |  +++ / $$$  |  ++ / $$  |  ++ / $$
kvcache-miss |  ++ / $    |  ++ / $$  |   + / $
cold-starts  |  ++ / $    |   + / $   |  ++ / $
tenant-io   |   + / $    |   + / $   |   + / $
network-jitter|  + / $    |   + / $   |   + / $

Interpretation notes (by row):
- session-mix: fast spikes amplify tail because long-turn sessions have priming sequences that inflate token generation CPU/GPU time; even small fractions of long sessions in the sample lead to large p99 shifts. This drives the biggest observed cost delta because longer sessions keep slots warm and block batching opportunities.
- kvcache-miss storms: observed during burst ramp when many new session contexts arrive; miss-rate climbs from ~5% -> ~38% which increases per-token compute and memory traffic. Turning kvcache off drops the miss-induced p99 but increases median and cost modestly due to more KV recomputation.
- cold-start waves: prewarm=false runs saw extra latency in first 120 seconds post-burst; adding prewarm cut that tail by ~40% but increased baseline cost by ~8%.
- tenant-io: softer but nonzero effect; when a noisy tenant is co-located we observe slot preemption events that bump tail by ~10–15% p99.

Tiny ascii charts (latency over time, fast-spike replicate):
Time(s)   p50(ms)  p95(ms)  p99(ms)  notes
0         45       120      210
5         50       180      980    <-- spike onset (session-mix dominated)
10        60       220     1200    <-- kvcache miss compounding
20        48       140      260    <-- decay toward baseline

Cost vs latency compact table (sustained surge, 90s):
Scenario            | tokens | total $ | $ / 1k tokens | p99(ms) median
baseline            | 1.1M   | 0.88    | 0.80          | 240
prewarm=true        | 1.0M   | 0.95    | 0.95          | 150
prewarm=false       | 1.15M  | 0.82    | 0.71          | 340
kvcache=off         | 1.05M  | 0.93    | 0.89          | 260
tenant-isolation=soft| 1.12M | 0.90    | 0.80          | 280

Quick takeaways for product/risk:
- For low-latency tiers: prewarm option + stricter session-length caps reduce p99 at modest steady-state cost increase. Recommend opt-in prewarm for "interactive-sla" customers.
- For cost-sensitive tiers: enable aggressive KV-cache sizing + adaptive eviction to avoid miss storms; consider lighter quant for median reduction.
- For multi-tenant pools: enforce soft isolation (slot reservations) during detected ramp windows; pre-schedule noisy-tenant throttles.

Action items (short list):
- (A1) Migrate the burst-detection alert to include KV-cache miss-rate as a primary signal (owner: Jin). due 2025-01-22.
- (A2) Add an E2E replay harness that can synthetic-mix session lengths (owner: Miguel). due 2025-02-02.
- (A3) Roll a short experiment toggling prewarm=true for 10% of latency-critical customers and measure cost uplift (owner: Aisha). due 2025-01-31.

Open questions / unknowns: 
- What is the break-even cost delta for prewarm across different model families? (need RB tests on 13B and 70B).
- How does network oversubscription in edge regions interact with KV-cache miss storms? We saw hints but not controlled data.
- Can the runtime detect early signs of session-mix-driven tail (e.g., proportion of long sessions in the last 30s) and trigger adaptive batching caps?

Notes to self / for handoff: 
- Link to replay harness prototype: github PR in linked_artifacts.
- Keep heatmap compact — this doc should be clipped to fit in a 1-page reviewer note on PagerDuty incident summaries.
- Will convert to slides if A1/A3 show clear delta.

End of working note.
